messages:
Maya: quick heads-up — ran a focused bakeoff this morning: weight-only INT8 via bitsandbytes vs llm.int8 path on Aurora-13B. wanted to surface surprising perf/quality tradeoffs.

Jonathan: nice — what's the test harness?

Maya: small: 1) 2k prompt eval set (mix short/long), 2) rouge/EM heuristics + pairwise human checks on 200 slices, 3) latency/throughput on p4d-like nodes with batch=4 and batch=16 for tail.

Ashok: which quant paths exactly? bnb 8bit vs llm.int8 (w-only)? any GPTQ/AWQ runs?

Maya: ran three configs: 
- baseline FP16 native
- bitsandbytes 8bit weight-only (bnb w8)
- llm.int8 weight-only (llmint8)
Also did a tiny GPTQ dump for 200-sample sanity but not full. AWQ deferred.

Elena: results? numbers pls :eyes:

Maya: TL;DR — both w-only quantizations save ~38-44% GPU memory and improve throughput ~1.25-1.45x depending on batch. But quality deltas diverge: bnb shows 1.8% drop on our accuracy metric, lllmint8 closer to 0.7% on same slices. latency median: bnb slightly faster for small batches, lllmint8 wins for larger batches due to less decode overhead.

Samir: can you paste the micro-benchmarks?

Maya: sure — median per-token latency (ms) on p4d-sim: 
```
batch=1: FP16 28.4 | bnb 25.1 | lllmint8 26.2
batch=4: FP16 21.0 | bnb 17.8 | lllmint8 16.9
batch=16: FP16 16.5 | bnb 13.8 | lllmint8 12.1
```

Jonathan: interesting that bnb beats lllmint8 at batch=1. could be kernel fusion?

Ashok: bnb has a faster int8 matmul kernel for tiny sequences; lllmint8's memory layout favors batched GEMMs. Also check KV cache alignment and padding.

Maya: noted — saw more variance in 1-token tail latency for lllmint8 but mean lower at larger bs. Also memory mapping: bnb uses 8-bit per weight with different packing; lllmint8 keeps some FP16 anchors which helped accuracy on instruction prompts.

Elena: what about quality numbers — can you share metric breakdown?

Maya: accuracy metric = task EM across multi-choice + code snippets. Numbers vs FP16 baseline: 
```
EM change: bnb -1.8% absolute (sd 0.6) | lllmint8 -0.7% abs (sd 0.4)
Perplexity change: bnb +6.2% | lllmint8 +2.1%
Human A/B prefer baseline over bnb 63% of pairs, baseline over lllmint8 52%.
```

Samir: hmm, 1.8% EM drop might be borderline for some customers. Did you try calibration tricks?

Maya: ran weight rescaling and percentile clipping on bnb (10k-sample calibration) — moved EM from -1.8% to -1.2% but latency hit +4% due to extra preprocessing. lllmint8 improved marginally with per-channel centering.

Jonathan: any decoding artifacts? hallucinations, tokenization mismatches?

Maya: a couple of edge cases: bnb produced occasional truncation on long context when attention scores hit clipping thresholds — appears as early eos. lllmint8 had softer outputs meaning more verbosity but fewer truncations.

Ashok: did you test multi-query/key-value packing differences? some backends assume grouped heads which affect cache footprint.

Maya: yes — single-head grouping mismatch caused ~5% throughput regression on bnb for quilled models. lllmint8 unaffected. Patch: added a translation shim to reorder KV layout — restored perf.

Elena: CI-bot — any flakiness in tests?

CI-bot: ran 2379123456_pipe: 18/20 unit slices passed; 2 flakies re: tokenizer edgecases. Logs: /ci/runs/2379123456.

Samir: what's our recommendation for rollout? conservative: lllmint8 default, bnb as fallback for low-latency single-token usecases?

Maya: I recommend: 
- Default routing to lllmint8 for batch-heavy endpoints (better quality & large-batch perf)
- Route to bnb for single-token low-latency paths (chat streaming) with added clipping guard and EOS detection
- Add canary with 10% traffic for 48h and auto-roll-back on >1% EM regression in slice monitors

Jonathan: agree. also add quant-calibration job in onboarding pipeline and surface per-model expected EM delta in the catalog UI.

Elena: can you add the run artifacts to model card? we need the perf/quality deltas + calibration flags.

Maya: on it — uploading artifacts and short playbook. Will ping when ready. cc @Elena @Ashok for review. :thumbsup:

Samir: nice work — thanks. small follow-up: schedule AWQ/GPTQ full bakeoff next week?

Maya: scheduled a 3-day run Wed-Fri. I'll post a separate thread with config matrix.

Jonathan: perfect — thanks Maya.
